fullPassage: As a teacher, you will hear pupils being labelled by other teachers, and there are a lot of labels that employed. If the label is a positive one, then that is fine and should be encouraged. Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly motivated and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will surrender to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a naughty little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively affecting and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them and reaffirming that label at every turn.

questions.passage: As a teacher, you will hear pupils being labelled by other teachers, and there are a lot of labels that employed. If the label is a (A)[positive / negative] one, then that is fine and should be encouraged. Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly motivated and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a (B)[disruptive / supportive] influence, he will surrender to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a (C)[naughty / obedient] little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively affecting and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them and reaffirming that label at every turn.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) positive(긍정적인), (B) disruptive(방해가 되는), (C) naughty(말 안 듣는) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
✅ ① positive — disruptive — naughty: 원문 그대로
❌ ② negative — disruptive — naughty: negative는 positive의 반의어 — '꼬리표가 긍정적이면 좋다'는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ positive — supportive — naughty: supportive(지지하는)는 disruptive(방해하는)의 반의어
❌ ④ positive — disruptive — obedient: obedient(순종하는)는 naughty(말 안 듣는)의 반의어
det.tip: positive↔negative, disruptive↔supportive, naughty↔obedient

questions.passage: As a teacher, you will hear pupils being labelled by other teachers, and there are a lot of labels that employed. If the label is a positive one, then that is fine and should be encouraged. Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly (A)[motivated / indifferent] and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will (B)[surrender / resist] to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a naughty little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively affecting and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them and (C)[reaffirming / questioning] that label at every turn.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) motivated(의욕 있는/동기부여 된), (B) surrender(굴복하다), (C) reaffirming(재확인하다) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① indifferent — surrender — reaffirming: indifferent(무관심한)는 motivated(동기부여 된)의 반의 뉘앙스 — '동기부여가 낮은 학생'이 꼬리표가 붙는 맥락
✅ ② motivated — surrender — reaffirming: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ motivated — resist — reaffirming: resist(저항하다)는 surrender(굴복하다)의 반의어
❌ ④ motivated — surrender — questioning: questioning(의문 품기)은 reaffirming(재확인)의 반의 뉘앙스
det.tip: motivated↔indifferent(동기부여↔무관심), surrender↔resist(굴복↔저항)

questions.passage: As a teacher, you will hear pupils being (A)[labelled / praised] by other teachers, and there are a lot of labels that employed. If the label is a positive one, then that is fine and should be encouraged. Sadly that is a (B)[rarity / norm]; it is the poorly motivated and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will surrender to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a naughty little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively (C)[affecting / ignoring] and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them and reaffirming that label at every turn.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) labelled(꼬리표가 붙은), (B) rarity(드문 일), (C) affecting(영향을 미치는) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① praised — rarity — affecting: praised(칭찬받은)는 labelled의 자리인데 긍정적 변형 — 꼬리표 붙는 맥락과 불일치
❌ ② labelled — norm — affecting: norm(일반적인 것)은 rarity(드문 일)의 반의어 — 긍정 꼬리표는 드물다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ labelled — rarity — ignoring: ignoring(무시)은 affecting(영향 미치기)의 반의어 — '긍정적 영향이 필요하다'는 맥락과 반대
✅ ④ labelled — rarity — affecting: 원문 그대로
det.tip: labelled↔praised(꼬리표↔칭찬), rarity↔norm(드묾↔보통), affecting↔ignoring(영향↔무시). 지문 등장 순서: (A)첫문장→(B)세번째문장→(C)마지막문장.

Sadly that is a ④<u>rarity</u>; it is the poorly motivated and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will surrender to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a naughty little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively affecting and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them and reaffirming that label at every turn.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 두 번째 밑줄 negative(부정적인)는 원문 positive(긍정적인)의 반의어 — '꼬리표가 긍정적이면 권장되어야 한다'는 맥락과 정반대
det.analysis:
✅ labelled: 원문 일치 — 학생들이 교사들에 의해 꼬리표가 붙는다
❌ negative: 원문 positive 자리에 반의어 대체 — 긍정 꼬리표는 장려해야 한다는 맥락과 반대 ←정답
✅ encouraged: 원문 일치 — 긍정 꼬리표는 장려되어야 함
✅ rarity: 원문 일치 — 긍정 꼬리표는 드문 일
det.tip: if the label is a positive one → should be encouraged. positive→negative 반의어 구분.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ constructive(건설적인)는 원문 disruptive(방해가 되는)의 반의어 — '수업을 방해하는 영향력'이라는 맥락과 정반대
det.analysis:
✅ ① poorly: 원문 일치 — poorly motivated(동기부여가 낮은)
✅ ② self-disciplined: 원문 일치 — poorly self-disciplined(자기 통제력이 낮은)
❌ ③ constructive: 원문 disruptive의 자리인데 반의어 — '방해하는 영향'이 '건설적인 영향'이 될 수는 없음
✅ ④ surrender: 원문 일치 — 꼬리표에 굴복하다
det.tip: disruptive influence = 방해가 되는 영향력. constructive(건설적)는 정반대 의미.

det.korean: ② negatively(부정적으로)는 원문 positively(긍정적으로)의 반의어 — '우리는 학생들에게 긍정적인 영향을 미쳐야 한다'는 맥락과 반대
det.analysis:
✅ ① constantly: 원문 일치 — 모두를 끊임없이 힘들게 한다
❌ ② negatively: 원문 positively의 자리인데 반의어 — 학생들을 긍정적으로 변화시켜야 한다는 주제와 정반대
✅ ③ sticking: 원문 일치 — 꼬리표를 붙이다
✅ ④ reaffirming: 원문 일치 — 꼬리표를 재확인하다
det.tip: positively affecting = 긍정적으로 영향 미치기. negatively는 반의어.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: encouraged(장려되다/권장되다) — 긍정적 꼬리표는 '장려'되어야 한다는 맥락. 뒤에 Sadly와 대비 구조.
det.analysis:
✅ ① encouraged: 원문 일치 — if the label is a positive one, it should be encouraged
❌ ② ignored: 무시되다, 긍정 꼬리표를 장려하는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ removed: 제거되다, 꼬리표 제거와 장려는 다름
❌ ④ criticized: 비판되다, 긍정 꼬리표를 비판할 이유 없음
det.tip: positive label → should be encouraged(장려되어야 함). Sadly로 이어지며 부정 꼬리표의 문제점 대비.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: surrender(굴복하다/항복하다) — 학생이 꼬리표(title)에 굴복하여 그 역할 그대로 된다는 맥락. 꼬리표의 자기충족적 예언.
det.analysis:
❌ ① escape: 도망치다, 꼬리표에 대한 저항 의미 — 텍스트의 '더욱 그렇게 된다'는 방향과 반대
❌ ② forget: 잊다, 꼬리표를 잊고 다른 행동 → 문장 흐름과 맞지 않음
✅ ③ surrender: 굴복하다 — 원문 일치. 꼬리표에 굴복하여 그대로 됨
❌ ④ transform: 변화시키다, 학생이 꼬리표를 변화시킨다는 의미 — 맥락 불일치
det.tip: surrender to the title = 꼬리표에 굴복하다. 자기충족적 예언의 핵심 동사.

det.korean: influence(영향/영향력) — disruptive influence(방해가 되는 영향력). 학생의 행동이 수업에 미치는 영향을 꼬리표로 붙이는 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ① student: 학생, '방해가 되는 학생'도 말이 되나 원문과 다르며 너무 단순
✅ ② influence: 영향력 — 원문 일치. disruptive influence = 방해가 되는 영향력
❌ ③ problem: 문제, '방해가 되는 문제'는 어색한 조합
❌ ④ failure: 실패, 방해와 실패는 다른 개념

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>rarity</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: rarity(드문 일/희귀한 것) = exception(예외/드문 경우)
det.analysis:
✅ ① exception: 예외/드문 경우, 동의어 — 긍정 꼬리표는 예외적인 드문 일
❌ ② custom: 관습, 자주 일어나는 것 — 반의 뉘앙스
❌ ③ standard: 표준/일반적인 것, 반의어 뉘앙스
❌ ④ option: 선택지, rarity와 무관
det.tip: rarity = something that rarely happens. exception(예외, 드문 경우)이 동의어.

det.korean: disruptive(방해가 되는/혼란을 일으키는) = troublesome(말썽을 일으키는/문제를 야기하는)
det.analysis:

❌ ③ creative: 창의적인, 반대 뉘앙스
❌ ④ helpful: 도움이 되는, 반의어
det.tip: disruptive = troublesome(문제 일으키는, 방해되는). disrupt(방해하다) + -ive.

det.analysis:
❌ ① accept: 받아들이다 — surrender와 유사한 방향(순응)

❌ ③ confirm: 확인하다 — 무관
✅ ④ resist: 저항하다, 반의어 — 꼬리표에 굴복하는 것의 반대

det.korean: reaffirming(재확인하다/재강조하다) ↔ challenging(도전하다/의문을 제기하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① challenging: 의문을 제기하다/도전하다, 반의어 — 꼬리표를 재확인하는 것의 반대는 꼬리표에 의문을 제기하는 것
❌ ② repeating: 반복하다 — reaffirming(재확인, 재강조)과 유사한 방향
❌ ③ strengthening: 강화하다 — reaffirming과 유사한 방향
❌ ④ maintaining: 유지하다 — reaffirming과 유사한 방향
det.tip: reaffirming(재확인, 재강조) ↔ challenging(의문 제기, 도전). re- = 다시, affirm = 확인하다.

questions.passage:
(A) The police officer told the suspect to <u>surrender</u> his weapon immediately.

(B) As a teacher, if you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will <u>surrender</u> to the title and become it even more.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 <u>surrender</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) surrender = 내놓다/제출하다(무기를 건네다), (B) surrender = 굴복하다(꼬리표에 따르다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 굴복하다 — (B) 내놓다: (A)는 무기를 건네는 것(내놓다), (B)는 꼬리표에 굴복하는 것 — 반대로 바뀜
❌ ② 둘 다 내놓다: (B)의 surrender to the title은 굴복 의미
✅ ③ (A) 내놓다 — (B) 굴복하다: 맥락별 의미 정확 구분
❌ ④ 둘 다 굴복하다: (A)의 surrender his weapon은 물건을 내주는 의미
det.tip: surrender his weapon(무기를 내놓다) vs surrender to the title(꼬리표에 굴복하다). 목적어 vs to+명사 구분.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the quality of being able to control one's behavior and impulses through one's own efforts"

det.korean: self-disciplined(자기 통제력이 있는) — 자신의 노력으로 행동과 충동을 통제하는 능력을 가진.
det.analysis:
❌ ① motivated: 동기부여 된, 통제력과는 다른 개념(욕구/의욕)
❌ ② encouraged: 장려된, 외부 자극에 의한 것
❌ ③ labelled: 꼬리표가 붙은, 통제력과 무관
✅ ④ self-disciplined: 정의 일치 — 스스로 행동/충동을 통제하는 자기 훈련
det.tip: self-disciplined = 자기 통제력이 있는. self-(스스로) + discipline(훈련/통제).

questions.passage: These are the very pupils we need to be __________ (affect) and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

These are the very pupils we need to be __________ (affect).

det.korean: affect(동사원형) → affecting(현재분사/동명사): be + V-ing 구조. '우리가 긍정적으로 영향을 미쳐야 할' 맥락.
det.analysis: be + V-ing → affecting (진행 또는 동명사). 'need to be affecting' = 영향을 미치고 있어야 할. 원형 affect는 'to be affect'가 되어 어색.
det.tip: be + -ing: need to be affecting(영향을 미치고 있어야 함). affect → affecting.

overlay.excerptSentences: These are the very pupils we need to be __________ (affect) and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them.

questions.passage: Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly __________ (motivate) and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

it is the poorly __________ (motivate) pupils who end up being labelled.

det.korean: motivate(동사원형) → motivated(과거분사/형용사): poorly motivated = 동기부여가 낮은. 부사 poorly의 수식을 받는 형용사.
det.analysis: poorly + 과거분사 → motivated (형용사적 과거분사). 'poorly motivated pupils' = 동기부여가 낮은 학생들. motivating(능동)은 '동기를 부여하는' 의미로 주어가 되어야 함.
det.tip: poorly motivated = 동기부여가 낮은. -ed 형용사(수동/상태) vs -ing 형용사(능동/원인) 구분.

overlay.excerptSentences: Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly __________ (motivate) and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled.

questions.passage: As a teacher, you will hear pupils being labelled by other teachers, and there are a lot of labels that employed. If the label is a positive one, then that is fine and should be encouraged. Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly motivated and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often end up being labelled. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will surrender to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a naughty little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively affecting and we will not achieve that by __________ and reaffirming that label at every turn.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: sticking a label on them(그들에게 꼬리표를 붙임으로써) — 꼬리표 붙이기로는 긍정적 영향을 이룰 수 없다는 본문의 핵심 주장.
det.analysis:
❌ ① praising their efforts sincerely: 진심으로 칭찬하기 — 효과적인 방법이라 'will not achieve'와 연결되면 의미 충돌
❌ ② giving them extra homework: 추가 과제 주기 — 본문 주제와 무관
❌ ③ reporting them to parents: 학부모에게 보고 — 본문 주제와 무관
✅ ④ sticking a label on them: 원문 일치 — 꼬리표를 붙여서는 긍정적 변화를 이룰 수 없음
det.tip: we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them = 꼬리표로는 안 된다. 본문의 핵심 주장.

questions.passage: As a teacher, you will hear pupils being labelled by other teachers, and there are a lot of labels that employed. If the label is a positive one, then that is fine and should be encouraged. Sadly that is a rarity; it is the poorly motivated and poorly self-disciplined pupils who often __________. Eventually the pupil becomes the label. If you tell a pupil often enough that he is a disruptive influence, he will surrender to the title and become it even more. If you tell a pupil that she is a naughty little girl who constantly makes it difficult for everyone, she will eventually become that even more. These are the very pupils we need to be positively affecting and we will not achieve that by sticking a label on them and reaffirming that label at every turn.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: end up being labelled(결국 꼬리표가 붙게 되다) — 동기부여가 낮고 자기 통제력이 낮은 학생들이 '결국 꼬리표가 붙는다'는 맥락. 부정 꼬리표의 대상이 되는 과정.
det.analysis:
❌ ① improve their academic performance: 학업 성취를 높이다 — 꼬리표가 붙는 학생과 반대 방향
❌ ② develop their self-confidence: 자신감 발달 — 꼬리표 피해자와 반대 방향
✅ ③ end up being labelled: 원문 일치 — 동기/자제력 낮은 학생들이 꼬리표가 붙는 결과
❌ ④ seek help from their teachers: 교사에게 도움 구하기 — 본문 흐름과 무관
det.tip: poorly motivated + poorly self-disciplined → end up being labelled. '결국 ~하게 된다' = end up V-ing.
